speech: Our seven-year-old with moderate eczema just tested positive for dust mite allergies.
Here's what nobody told us to do.
Now most parents don't know this, but a cough, itchy skin, or a stuffy nose that only shows up at
night and only at home can be a sign of a dust mite allergy. If they're fine at grandmas,
fine on holiday, but wake up stuffy and tired at home, that's your clue.
It's coming from their bed. Now what if the best thing you can do starts inside the mattress
instead of only washing the sheets on hot and hoping? You need to deal with the source,
the dust mites living in their mattress, and what they leave behind.
This might sound unusual, but over 30,000 homes already do it by slipping a small card under the
mattress. And let me tell you, parents love how easy it is. Nothing to spray on their bedding,
no smell, nothing to plug in. A plant-derived pheromone lure pulls dust mites out of hiding,
and the adhesive holds them on the card. The lure works from up to 50 centimeters away,
so mites come to the card from across the mattress, away from where they lay their heads all night,
so they can't breathe it in. When it's time, pull the card out, full of mites, straight in the bin,
clean one in. So if you've ever laid awake listening to that cough and wondered what else you can do,
you haven't missed anything. Now you can take it out of their bed.
